text: The Wind Shot (Japanese: , Uindoshotto) is a weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is one of Sharla's ether rifles.

White Clusters (Japanese: , Howaitokurasutā) are weapons in . They are rifles wielded by Sharla. They can be acquired by trading with Ewan who can be found in the Ether Mine. It can also be obtained as a Quest reward.

The Warrior Gnasher (Japanese: , Senshi no Tsukutsuku) is a Biter weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is obtained during An Errand for the Heropon before Riki joins the party, and can only be used by him. It is not available from any other sources.
The Will-o'-Wisp Staff (Japanese: , Shiranui no Tsue) is a weapon in . It is one of Melia's staves.
The Windmill Pavilion (Japanese: , Kazeoi no Fūshagoya) is a landmark in . It is located in Makna Forest, at the south end of the elevated walkways the Nopon use, and north of Abyss Basin.

The Waypoint Beacon (Japanese: , Michishirube no Kagaribi) is a landmark in . It is located in Makna Forest, in the area between Bridge One and Bridge Two. A Bagrus Nebula can often be found floating here, as well as several Makna Feris in all directions.
Wet Hair (Japanese: , Shimetta ke) is a common material in . It can be obtained from low-level Bunnivs in Tephra Cave, or traded for.

White Hoxes (Japanese: , Arubumu Hoggusu, Album Hox) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Hox family, and can be found at level 75 on Bionis' Leg, on top of the brown platforms that are on top of Raguel Lake. They are usually accompanied by Dark Hoxes. They can drop the Hox Daylight Spur needed for Replica Monado 3 and Colony 6 Reconstruction.

The Weapon Development Lab (Japanese: , Heiki Kaihatsu-kyoku Kenkyū-tō) is a location in , located in the Military District in Colony 9. This is Shulk's workplace. In this lab, special investigations have been taking place with the Monado at their core focus. The place is semi-trashed when Reyn accidentally activates the Monado and Fiora is nearly injured.
The White Radiant is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is one of the four Radiants required for Ancient Ceremony Offerings in Satorl Marsh. It is found at Basin Cave in Satorl Marsh.

What is Love?! (Japanese: , Ren'ai wo Oshieteyaru) is a quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Ewan in Colony 6 at the Reconstruction HQ. If Sharla is in the active party, she will comment. If the Lake Drop is used to complete Imaginations Tempered at the Refugee Camp, this quest as well as What is Courage?! and Matryona's Answer will be unavailable.

What is Courage?! (Japanese: , Yūki wo Oshieteyaru) is a quest in . It can be received from Ewan in the Reconstruction HQ of Colony 6. If Sharla is in the active party, she will comment. Once this quest is completed, Matryona's Answer will be available.

Who is Bigger? (Japanese: , Docchi wo Ōkiku) is a quest in . It is triggered during the course of the objectives for the Getting Bigger! received from Dabidabi, after having spoken to Puko at the back side of the weapon shop at Kyn Shopping Street in Frontier Village.

White Smoke Hox (Japanese: , Hakuen no Hoggusu) are quest exclusive enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Hox family, and can be found on the Raguel Bridge during the mutually-exclusive quests To Colony 6! and The Road Home. Six of them must be defeated in order to complete either quest.

The White Spider Heart is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is obtained during The Blood of Bafalgar in Tephra Cave and is dropped by the Dazzling Tolosnia. It must be then offered up at the Sacrificial Altar to open access to the Prayer Room.

Wind Nebulae are enemies in . They are members of the Nebula family, and can be found at level 26 in Satorl Marsh anytime but with no fog. A group of them can be found in the water southeast of the Glowing Obelisk.

Willow Bunnivs (Japanese: , Wirō Banīvu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Bunniv family, and can be found at level 6 in Tephra Cave past Tephra Path, in the side passages near the Caterpile Nest, and at the Mag Mell Ruins. One of these enemies must be defeated to complete Monster Quest 4 - Part 1.

Wind Vangs are enemies in . They are members of the Vang family, and can be found at level 9 in Tephra Cave. They can be found near the Spring of Grief. Defeating five of them is required to complete the quest A Young Captain's Suffering given by Emmy Leater in Colony 9.

Whapol Sardis are fish-like enemies in . They are members of the Sardi family, and can be found in the Eks Watering Hole in Makna Forest. Defeating two of them is required to complete the Frontier Village's quest Monster Quest 1 - Part 2. In Future Connected, defeating three of them is required to complete Evelen on the Edge.

Watcher Hodes are enemies in . They are members of the Hode family, and can be found at level 34 in the Hode Refuge at the Eryth Sea. They can drop Luxury Hode Woods, three pieces of which are needed for the quest Mend the Plant.
The Wedding Ring is a Key Item in . It is the object of Search Quest 1 in Colony 9. It can be found behind Dunban's house.

White Brog Livers are rare materials in . They can only be dropped by Detox Brogs in Satorl Marsh, or traded for with Bokoko. According to their description, they are succulent white livers that contain a juice that is so white it shines. Three White Brog Livers are needed for Cook-Off Counter Attack!.
The Water Ether Crystals are a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. Obtaining them is the objective of Mystery Girl Rescue. They can be found near an Ether crystal deposit at Lakeside in Makna Forest.

Weak Berryjammy (Japanese: , Byōjakuna Sutorojamu) is a quest in . It can be received from Norara at a balcony of a building from the Reconstruction HQ, only after Perrine and Berryjammy have been invited to Colony 6. If Reyn is in the active party, he will comment. Obstinate Berryjammy will be triggered upon completing this quest. This quest and Cursed Berryjammy are mutually exclusive. Cursed Berryjammy will be offered in place of this quest if Mefimefi was invited to Colony 6 instead of Perrine.
Wings of Light are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are dropped by Telethia in Bionis' Interior.

We Made It (Japanese: , Nakama wa Ikiteiru) is a Story Quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is received automatically at the Zakt Spring after the story events involving Fiora joining back by completing Reunion with Fiora.

The Weapon Creation Machine is an object in . It is found in the Control Tower of the Central Factory. It is activated by the Weapon Creation Panel and is used in order to create weapons. It is first used for the story quest Find a Path to the Top, creating the Time Bomb to explode the Factory Vent. It is used again during New Weapon for Fiora to make the War Blades for Fiora.

The Weapon Creation Panel is a mechanical object in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is found in the Maintenance Wing of the Central Factory. It activates the Weapon Creation Machine and is needed to make the Time Bomb for Find a Path to the Top, and later the War Blades for New Weapon for Fiora.

Watching Over Them (Japanese: , Mimamorumono-tachi, The Attentive Watchers) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located in the Residential District in Colony 9, between Dunban and Reyn at pink affinity. It can only be viewed at night, and after the Mechon attack on the colony.

What's On Reyn's Mind (Japanese: , Rain ga Kinishiteru Koto) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located in a small cavern within the Refugee Camp on Bionis' Leg, between Sharla and Reyn at green affinity.

What Visions May Bring (Japanese: , Miraishi ga Moratasu Mono) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located just north of Raguel Bridge on the Bionis' Leg, between Sharla and Shulk at green affinity. This Heart-to-Heart is unlocked after events in the Ether Mine.
The West Janpath Plain (Japanese: , Janpasu-ko no Nishi Heigen) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Primordia, west of Janpath Lake.

Winged Viper (known as Sword Fang in the Japanese version) is a Class featured in . This class provides bonuses to melee accuracy, ranged accuracy, and evasion. It is one of two classes that can be leveled up from Commando and can be leveled up to Full Metal Jaguar. The playable characters of this class include Phog, whereas Murderess's class is an Alternative Winged Viper.

The Weapon Material is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is received from one of the Junks Staff when New Weapon for Fiora is accepted. It can be used at the Weapon Creation Machine to make War Blades for Fiora.

Where the Ancestors Sleep (祖霊の眠る地) is a Field Track in Xenoblade Chronicles, composed and arranged by Manami Kiyota. It is track 24 of disc 3 from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack. This music is heard while the party is inside the High Entia Tomb.

Wasteland Evellos (Japanese: , Weisuto Sutorutto) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Evello family, and can be found at level 14-19 around FN Site 302 and the North Coast in Oblivia during the day. Five of them must be defeated during Evello Eradication.

Whirling Terebras (Japanese: , Tān Rutoru, Turn Lutru) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Terebra family. They can be found at level 21-24 at West Janpath Plain and near Janpath Lake, or near Sayram Lake in Primordia.
The Water Purification Plant (Japanese: , Jōsuijō) is a landmark in . It is located in the Residential District of New Los Angeles, near the entrance to the Administrative District.
We Were Soldiers (Japanese: , Gengunjin, Ex-Military) is a Affinity Mission in . It can be received from the BLADE Barracks in New Los Angeles.

Welkin Levitath (Japanese: , Werukin Rukiora) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Levitath family, and can be found at level 43 at South Janpath Plain, Talon Rock Second Terrane, and East Janpath Plain, level 44 above Tallpach Peak and Sickle Rock Rise only at night, level 45 at Silent Mire, level 47 at Talon Rock Second Terrane, and level 49 at Talon Rock Third Terrane in Primordia. They are sight enemies if the party is in a Skell, but non-aggressive otherwise. Two of them must be defeated during Two Warriors.

The Whimsical Duoguill (Japanese: , Wimu Guira) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Duoguill family. It is found at level 9 at Janpath Lake in Primordia only during Myles to Go.

The West Gate Plain (Japanese: , Uesuto Gēto no Heigen) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Primordia, outside the western entrance to New Los Angeles. Cross and Elma fight a horde of Young Grexes here before entering New Los Angeles for the first time.

West Melville Street (Japanese: , Mobī Sutorīto Nishi) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located at the west end of the Commercial District, near the entrance to the Industrial District. Army Pizza and Pauline's Rosemoss Restaurant are located along this street.

Whale's Gullet (Japanese: , Kujira no Nodo) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a cave located in Noctilum, north of Rustpool Banks. It can be accessed from the Rustpool Banks or the Whale's Weeper. A Raging Simius guards the entrance. Angry Simius and Striker Simius dwell inside.

The Whale's Nostril BC (Japanese: , Kujira no Bikō-mae BC) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Noctilum, north of FN Site 222 and east of Rust Lake, at the southern entrance to the Whale's Nostril. The camp is primarily operated by the Curators.

The Whale's Nostril (Japanese: , Kujira no Bikō) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a large cavern in Noctilum, north of the Whale's Nostril BC and southwest of FN Site 221. After accepting The Ties That Bind, the Dodonga Caravan can be found at the southern entrance. Easily Acessible with Old Dragontail Tree landmark.
Welcome Back, Conner (Japanese: , Yukuefumei no Konā, Conner the Missing) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Nathan at East Gate Plain in Primordia.

Wild Mephites (Japanese: , Wirudā Mepitesu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Mephite family, and can be found at level 16-20 at Aaroy Plain or south of FN Site 306 in Oblivia.
Wendy (Japanese: , Wedi) is a NPC in and . She can be found at Ishmael Hills in the Residential District of New Los Angeles at daytime.
Western Suids (Japanese: , Wesuto Zūsu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Suid family, and can be found at level 16-20 north of Oblivia's Twin Arches.

Wind Auravises (Japanese: , Windo Akuira) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Auravis family, and can be found at level 23 in the Suncatch Ravine and at level 21-22 above Rustpool Banks in Noctilum during the day.

White Progen (Japanese: , Howaito Ekuusu) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Progen family and can be found at level 19-20 at the Seabird's Beak or Cleansing Spring in Sylvalum. Two must be defeated to complete Bottoms Up.
Wayward Weather is a Soul Voice in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is triggered when the weather changes during a battle.

White Ovis (Japanese: , Howaito Owisu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Ovis family, and can be found at level 22-29 in Sylvalum, near FN Site 415. Five of them must be defeated during Offing Ovis (White).

Waterway Tangle (Japanese: , Mayoi Suidō) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Noctilum, east of the Whale's Nostril. The Ensanguined Font and Lakeview Stronghold can be found at the north end of the river.
Wersal (Japanese: , Weryusaryu) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She is a Ma-non and can be found in the Commercial District between Central Melville Street and Barista Court.
The West Ciel Sandsea (Japanese: , Shieru-ko no Seibu Sakai) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Sylvalum, on the west side of Lake Ciel.

Welkin Auravises (Japanese: , Werukin Akuira) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Auravis family, and can be found at level 21-25 at FN Site 116 or Arendt Bridge, or at level 28-30 in Primordia. Two must be defeated to complete one route of That's In-Credible!.

West Ibra Ravine (Japanese: , Ibura Keikoku Seibu) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Oblivia. It is a narrow valley west of Central Ibra Ravine containing a pond and numerous vespers.

Water Woes (Japanese: , Biāno Jōsuijō no Kenzō, Construction of the Biahno Water Purification Plant) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be accepted from Ajoa at the Water Purification Plant in the Residential District of New Los Angeles. The Biahno Water-Purification Plant landmark is unlocked during this mission.
White Cometites are common Precious Resources in Xenoblade Chronicles X. Five are required for the affinity mission The Repair Job, if the player chooses to sympathize with Lin.

Whip Scorpions (Japanese: , Wippusukōpion) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Oblivia, in particular at Sea Whisper Valley located one segment south of FN Site 321 near the waterfalls. Four of them are needed for A Little Protection.

White Iron Sands (Japanese: , Shirasutetsu) are rare collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Primordia, commonly on the West Janpath Plain. Five units are required for the Normal Mission Training Day.
Will Peppers (Japanese: , Wirupīman) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Oblivia, on Aaroy Plain. Three of them are needed to complete the mission Popular Peppers.
White Cassises (Japanese: , Howaito Kashisu) are rare collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Sylvalum.
White Sand Beetles (Japanese: , Shirosunakorogashi) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Sylvalum.

White Mirrorglasses are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Grexes in Primordia, or for 30 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. Two are needed to complete Setting Forth. They are required for Visual Cloaking and Cloak.SIGHT augments.
White Blattas (Japanese: , Howaito Buratta) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Blatta family. They can be found at level 10 in Headwater Cavern in Primordia.

Wilbur (Japanese: , Wirūgu) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found beside a swimming pool in the Residential District's Ishmael Hills. After Trade Agreement, he becomes a member of the Harriers Division.
West Cinderdunes (Japanese: , Nishi no Kaijin Sakyū) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Sylvalum, west of the North Cinderdunes and the FN Site 410. The FN Site 407 is here.

Wenzel, the Inebriated (, Suikyō no Vātsurafu, lit. Whimsical Václav) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Saltat family. It can be found at level 70 at Cryptic Sign in Oblivia. It is aggressive during the day and non-aggressive during the night toward parties on foot, and non-aggressive toward Skells at all times.

Weight is an Armour stat in Xenoblade Chronicles, and is a measure of the amount by which the armour hinders the wearer's movement. The weight of equipped armour is subtracted from the wearer's Agility. This can be mitigated by certain skills which reduce the weight of armour. The weight stat is a combination of the armour's physical weight, bulkiness, and other characteristics which hinder the wearer's movement. For example, the Empress Mask is classified as Light Armour, but has a relatively high weight of 5, presumably because it restricts the wearer's sight.
What the Skell?! (Japanese: , Sutorenji Nova, Strange Nova) is an Affinity Mission in . It can be received near the Outfitters Test Hangar in the Industrial District of New Los Angeles.
Weapon Guard is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Samurai Gunner at rank 6.

White Forfex Shells are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from head parts of white Forfexes. Ten of them are needed during Off the Record (archaeological). They are components in all Ultrafauna Slayer and Slayer.ULTRAFAUNA augments.

Waste Not, Want Not (Japanese: , Zu Haggu Zangai Kaishū, Zu Pharg Wreckage Recovery) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Lara Mara inside the Hangar in the Administrative District. Although not a prerequisite, the Basic Mission Weapons Cleanup Crew can be used to locate this mission.
The Windshield Glass is an Important Item in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It must be collected during The Handy Ma-non on the East Gate Plain in Primordia.
Well-Weathered is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Mastermind at rank 4. Cross and Hope can use this skill.
Wikaye (Japanese: , Wikae) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She can be found at the Starboard of the Ma-non Ship in New Los Angeles.
What's a Taoman? is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from a meteorologist and the primary destination is Sylvalum.
Wazdo Tygant is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is a Tree Clan Prone and can be found at the Port Side of the Ma-non Ship in New Los Angeles during the night.
White Fungal Eggs are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Sylooth.

White Lifehold (Japanese: , Shiro no Raifupointo) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Lara Mara across from the AM Terminal in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles. Lara Mara's Basic Mission Top-Secret Mission can be used to locate it, but is not a prerequisite. The Communication Data is obtained upon completion of this mission.
White Scintimure Tentacles are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from white Scintimures in Sylvalum. They are components in Night.MR-ACC augments.

Weapons Cleanup Crew is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from Lara Mara and the primary destination is the Administrative District. This mission leads into Waste Not, Want Not, though accepting it is not a prerequisite.

What's a Rocambole? is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from a botanist and the primary destination is Oblivia. It can be accepted from the BLADE Concourse in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles.

White Meaty Caecus Livers are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from green Caecuses in Sylvalum, or for 82 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are components in SpecUp.APP-HP augments.

White Mortifole Feathers are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from white Mortifoles, or for 42 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are a component in Arts: Gain TP and Arts.GP augments.

White Sylooth Braces are unique materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from white Sylooth in Sylvalum, or for 114 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are components in creating X, XV, and XX Melee Attack Up and SpecUp.M-ATK augments.

White Yggralith Nuts are unique materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Pharsis, the Everqueen, or for 138 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are components in X, XV, and XX Cooldown Reducer and Custom.WP-SPEED augments.

White Yggralith Scales are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Pharsis, the Everqueen, or for 78 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are components in X, XV, and XX Critical Surge augments.

Watxes Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts Orphean Technologies Dual Swords. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission Ovah and Out. The Watxes weapons available in-game are: * Archetype Watxes * Iron Watxes * Carbide Watxes * Cermet Watxes * Chrome Watxes * Chromoly Watxes * Cobalt Watxes * Original Watxes * Titanium Watxes * Ceramic Watxes * Diamond Watxes

Wild Challenge is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.12, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting four Blaudolch, the Chalcedonys. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

Water Rights is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.13, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting sixteen Lophids. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

What's That Smell?! is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.13, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting twelve Mephites. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

Water Torture is a Support Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked when Chapter 12 is completed. It allows the player to quickly raise affinity with party members, and earn Division Points to raise one's BLADE Level. Enemies do not drop any items in this mission. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.
Weather Master is a ground armor anticlimate augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X that reduces the damage from harmful weather. The Skell equivalent is Weather.DAMAGE-RES.
Weather.FOG-RES is a Skell anticlimate armor augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It grants immunity to the effects of fog when in a Skell. The ground equivalent is Fog Screen.

Weather.HEAVY-RAIN-RES is a Skell armor anticlimate augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It grants immunity to the effects of heavy rain when in a Skell. It is the Skell equivalent of Heavy Rain Screen.
Weather.S-STORM-RES is a Skell armor anticlimate augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It grants immunity to the effects of sandstorms when in a Skell. It is the Skell equivalent of Sandstorm Screen.

Weather.EM-STORM-RES is a Skell armor anticlimate augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It grants immunity to the effects of electromagnetic storms when in a Skell. The ground equivalent is EM Storm Screen.
Weather.E-MIST-RES is a Skell armor anticlimate augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It grants immunity to the effects of energy mist while in a Skell. The ground equivalent is Energy Mist Screen.

Weather.RISING-E-MIST-RES is a Skell armor anticlimate augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It grants immunity to the effects of rising energy mist when in a Skell. It is the Skell equivalent of Rising Energy Mist Screen.
Weather.SPORE-RES is a Skell armor anticlimate augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It grants immunity to the effects of spore clouds when in a Skell. It is the Skell equivalent of Spore Screen.
Weather.DAMAGE-RES is a Skell armor anticlimate augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It reduces weather damage by 5% to 100% when in a Skell. It is the Skell equivalent of Weather Master.
